correctness.rationale: For B={|x|^p+|y|^q<=1} with 2<p<q, all Euclidean pullback norms arise from positive-definite quadratic forms Q and have squared distortion M(Q)/m(Q) on the Luxemburg sphere. Coordinate sign averages eliminate off-diagonal terms without worsening the two-sided quadratic comparison. For diagonal Q=diag(a,b) and t=|x|^p, the squared Hilbert norm is F(t)=a t^{2/p}+b(1-t)^{2/q}, strictly concave; its minimum is min(a,b) at an axis. Normalize this to one: a,b>=1, so any nonidentity diagonal form has strictly larger interior maximum than F_{1,1}. For Q=[[1,c],[c,1]] after sign average, nonzero c is excluded because opposite sign pairs at the unique interior maximum t_* produce a squared norm exceeding M_{p,q}, while axis minimum remains <=1. f(t)=t^{2/p}+(1-t)^{2/q} is strictly concave with derivative going from +infinity to -infinity; its unique stationary point is the displayed critical root. Independent p=4,q=6 scalar solve gives t_*=0.61977620919 and M=1.51171647247, consistent with the source and not used in the proof. Boundary p=2 and finite p<2 are explicitly excluded.
